sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: 2017 was a tough year.
sentences.zh: 2017年是艰难的一年。

sentences.en: Not my president!
sentences.zh: 这不是我的总统！

sentences.en: Not my...
sentences.zh: 这不是我的……

sentences.en: Okay, maybe that was an understatement.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许那话说得太轻了。

sentences.en: What he said 24 hours ago is a threat.
sentences.zh: 他24小时前说的话是一种威胁。

sentences.en: It's very serious.
sentences.zh: 这非常严重。

sentences.en: Should the world, and more importantly, should Kim Jong-un take that literally?
sentences.zh: 世界，更重要的是，金正恩应该照字面意思去理解吗？

sentences.en: Thoughtfulness isn't what shareholders are looking for, and it's not what voters look for.
sentences.zh: 深思熟虑并不是股东们所追求的，也不是选民们所看重的。

sentences.en: That is the unraveling of an informed democracy.
sentences.zh: 那是一个知情民主制度的瓦解。

sentences.en: Where was I?
sentences.zh: 我刚才说到哪儿了？

sentences.en: Oh yeah, we're all going to die.
sentences.zh: 哦对了，我们都要完蛋了。

sentences.en: Many Americans are angry.
sentences.zh: 许多美国人感到愤怒。

sentences.en: That anger has led to sadness and a fear that the United States is falling apart.
sentences.zh: 这种愤怒导致了悲伤，以及对美国正在分崩离析的恐惧。

sentences.en: After two centuries as a beacon of democracy,
sentences.zh: 在作为民主灯塔两个世纪之后，

sentences.en: many fear the ties that bind us together as a nation are starting to fray.
sentences.zh: 许多人担心将我们作为一个国家凝聚在一起的纽带正开始磨损。

sentences.en: Brexit has spurred secession talks all over the world, even in our own country.
sentences.zh: 英国脱欧在世界各地引发了脱离联邦的讨论，甚至在我们自己的国家也是如此。

sentences.en: That's what activists in the state of California want.
sentences.zh: 这就是加利福尼亚州活动人士想要的。

sentences.en: Ever since the election of President Trump, the campaign for Cal-exits...
sentences.zh: 自从特朗普总统当选以来，加州脱离联邦的运动……

sentences.en: At the time, several hundred people face-to-face in brawls, using sticks and rocks as weapons.
sentences.zh: 当时，数百人面对面发生冲突，使用棍棒和石块作为武器。

sentences.en: If you feel our nation is at a breaking point, today's show may provide you some solace.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得我们的国家正处于崩溃的边缘，今天的节目或许能给你带来一些慰藉。

sentences.en: Historian David Moss takes the long view.
sentences.zh: 历史学家大卫·莫斯采取了长远的眼光。

sentences.en: In his book, Democracy, a Case Study, David argues that intense political conflict,
sentences.zh: 在他的著作《民主：一个案例研究》中，大卫认为激烈的政治冲突，

sentences.en: to the point where it looks like our democracy is about to fail,
sentences.zh: 甚至到了看起来我们的民主即将失败的地步，

sentences.en: has been with us since the country was born.
sentences.zh: 自从这个国家诞生以来就一直伴随着我们。

sentences.en: In fact, he argues, such conflict, far from being a harbinger of doom,
sentences.zh: 事实上，他认为，这种冲突远非末日的预兆，

sentences.en: is actually a sign of vitality.
sentences.zh: 实际上是活力的标志。

sentences.en: I think we need to remember American democracy is far from perfect,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要记住，美国民主远非完美，

sentences.en: but it is extraordinarily resilient, and it has generated tremendous progress.
sentences.zh: 但它具有非凡的韧性，并产生了巨大的进步。

sentences.en: Many people judge political success or failure based on whether their side wins.
sentences.zh: 许多人根据他们支持的一方是否获胜来判断政治上的成功或失败。

sentences.en: David uses a different metric.
sentences.zh: 大卫使用了不同的衡量标准。

sentences.en: He says in the long term, real success and failure is about the health or sickness of democracy itself.
sentences.zh: 他说从长远来看，真正的成功与失败在于民主制度本身的健康与否。

sentences.en: Does conflict strengthen our bonds, or does it destroy the fabric that holds us together?
sentences.zh: 冲突是加强了我们的联系，还是摧毁了维系我们的结构？

sentences.en: In today's episode, we'll use American history as a lens to look at how conflict
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将以美国历史为视角，来看看冲突

sentences.en: can sometimes bring people together, and sometimes tear them apart.
sentences.zh: 有时如何将人们凝聚在一起，有时又如何将他们撕裂。

sentences.en: So, if you could, I would love to just get a level on your voice as we get started.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果可以的话，我想在我们开始之前先确认一下你的音量。

sentences.en: David and I met for an interview on the sidelines of a conference in Colorado.
sentences.zh: 大卫和我是在科罗拉多州的一次会议间隙会面进行采访的。

sentences.en: My producer Tara Boyle and I found a meeting room at our hotel for the interview.
sentences.zh: 我的制片人塔拉·博伊尔和我为采访在酒店找了一间会议室。

sentences.en: It wasn't quite studio quality, but it had a rustic charm to it.
sentences.zh: 它虽然算不上演播室级别，但有一种质朴的魅力。

sentences.en: I started by asking David the obvious question.
sentences.zh: 我首先问了大卫一个显而易见的问题。

sentences.en: At a time when political conflict seems to be pulling the country apart, how can he possibly be optimistic?
sentences.zh: 在政治冲突似乎正在撕裂国家的时候，他怎么可能保持乐观？

sentences.en: Certainly in the United States, conflict has been, not every time, but a lot of the time, very productive.
sentences.zh: 当然在美国，冲突并非每次，但很多时候是非常有建设性的。

sentences.en: And so I could give you many examples, maybe we could talk about some of them.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以给你举很多例子，也许我们可以谈谈其中一些。

sentences.en: But really, if you think about, for example, in the economic marketplace,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如果你想想，例如在经济市场中，

sentences.en: competition, conflict, is really what drives innovation, new ideas.
sentences.zh: 竞争和冲突，确实是推动创新和新思想的动力。

sentences.en: And the same thing happens in the political sphere.
sentences.zh: 同样的事情也发生在政治领域。

sentences.en: So you have, you know, you have two parties, you have different interest groups,
sentences.zh: 所以你有，你知道，你有两个政党，你有不同的利益集团，

sentences.en: you have all sorts of different people trying to fight it out.
sentences.zh: 你有各种各样的人试图争个高下。

sentences.en: And in the process, you get all sorts of good ideas that are surfaced.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，你会涌现出各种各样的好主意。

sentences.en: And so conflict, competition in the political marketplace is crucial.
sentences.zh: 所以冲突，政治市场中的竞争是至关重要的。

sentences.en: David says that what matters is not whether there's conflict,
sentences.zh: 大卫说，重要的不是是否存在冲突，

sentences.en: but whether that conflict is constructive or destructive to democracy.
sentences.zh: 而是这种冲突对民主是有建设性的还是破坏性的。

sentences.en: If you just focus on the conflict, you might not see the real picture.
sentences.zh: 如果你只关注冲突本身，你可能看不到全貌。

sentences.en: To understand the effects of different kinds of conflict,
sentences.zh: 为了理解不同类型冲突的影响，

sentences.en: I asked David to tell me about three moments in American history
sentences.zh: 我请大卫给我讲讲美国历史上的三个时刻，

sentences.en: where political disagreements were so intense,
sentences.zh: 当时政治分歧如此激烈，

sentences.en: it seemed like the country might implode.
sentences.zh: 看起来国家可能会崩溃。

sentences.en: In one case, as we will see, it nearly did.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，在其中一个案例中，它几乎真的崩溃了。

sentences.en: The first moment was just a few years after the founding of the new nation.
sentences.zh: 第一个时刻是在新国家成立仅仅几年之后。

sentences.en: We think of today as being an unusually bitter moment in politics.
sentences.zh: 我们认为今天是一个政治上异常痛苦的时刻。

sentences.en: Donald Trump calls Hillary Clinton crooked Hillary,
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普称希拉里·克林顿为“狡诈的希拉里”，

sentences.en: while Democrats say Trump is unfit for office, possibly crazy.
sentences.zh: 而民主党人则称特朗普不适合担任公职，甚至可能疯了。

sentences.en: But the founding fathers were happy to sling mud too.
sentences.zh: 但开国元勋们也乐于互相抹黑。

sentences.en: Thomas Jefferson supporters called John Adams hideous and hermaphroditical.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·杰斐逊的支持者称约翰·亚当斯为“丑陋且雌雄同体”。

sentences.en: Adams called Alexander Hamilton that bastard brat of a Scottish peddler.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯称亚历山大·汉密尔顿为“那个苏格兰小贩的私生子”。

sentences.en: The nasty talk was hardly the worst of it.
sentences.zh: 恶毒的言论还远非最糟糕的部分。

sentences.en: There were deep disagreements about what it meant to be a country.
sentences.zh: 关于作为一个国家意味着什么，存在着深刻的分歧。

sentences.en: George Washington said he was mortified that political fighting
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿说，他感到非常羞愧，因为政治斗争

sentences.en: had left the country looking, quote,
sentences.zh: 让这个国家看起来，引用他的话，

sentences.en: ridiculous and contemptible.
sentences.zh: “荒谬且令人鄙视”。

sentences.en: It did appear to many, including Washington,
sentences.zh: 对许多人，包括华盛顿来说，确实看起来

sentences.en: that the country might be falling apart.
sentences.zh: 这个国家可能正在分崩离析。

sentences.en: So if you look at what was going on,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看看当时发生了什么，

sentences.en: this new nation had just, you know,
sentences.zh: 这个新国家刚刚，你知道，

sentences.en: they declared their independence in 1776.
sentences.zh: 他们在1776年宣布了独立。

sentences.en: And so, you know, they're jubilant about having won this battle.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他们为赢得了这场战斗而欢欣鼓舞。

sentences.en: But it turns out that things sort of turn south fairly quickly.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，情况很快就变糟了。

sentences.en: So, you know, within a few years of the formal end of the war,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在战争正式结束后的几年内，

sentences.en: you start seeing some very serious problems across the country.
sentences.zh: 你开始看到全国各地出现了一些非常严重的问题。

sentences.en: At the time, the new nation was not yet governed by our Constitution,
sentences.zh: 当时，新国家还不是由我们的宪法来治理的，

sentences.en: but by another document known as the Articles of Confederation.
sentences.zh: 而是由另一份被称为《邦联条例》的文件治理。

sentences.en: And they really made the states almost all-powerful.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上赋予了各州几乎全部的权力。

sentences.en: The states were sovereign.
sentences.zh: 各州拥有主权。

sentences.en: Federal government existed, but it was very weak.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府存在，但非常虚弱。

sentences.en: There was no president.
sentences.zh: 没有总统。

sentences.en: There was no Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 没有最高法院。

sentences.en: Just a Congress.
sentences.zh: 只有一个国会。

sentences.en: And the Congress had very limited power.
sentences.zh: 而且国会的权力非常有限。

sentences.en: For example, it could spend and it could borrow, but it couldn't tax.
sentences.zh: 例如，它可以支出和借款，但不能征税。

sentences.en: So it turns out that may not have been the best idea
sentences.zh: 所以事实证明这可能不是个好主意，

sentences.en: because the government does spend, especially on the war, and it does borrow.
sentences.zh: 因为政府确实有支出，特别是在战争期间，而且确实有借款。

sentences.en: But then, of course, it's not able to raise revenues.
sentences.zh: 但当然，它无法增加收入。

sentences.en: So the federal government is soon in default.
sentences.zh: 所以联邦政府很快就违约了。

sentences.en: They're not able to pay their creditors.
sentences.zh: 他们无法支付债权人。

sentences.en: And among the creditors who are most important are former soldiers.
sentences.zh: 而在最重要的债权人中，有前士兵们。

sentences.en: And so the soldiers aren't getting paid.
sentences.zh: 所以士兵们拿不到工资。

sentences.en: So that's a serious problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个严重的问题。

sentences.en: That's one thing going on.
sentences.zh: 这是一件正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: The states start putting tariffs on each other.
sentences.zh: 各州开始互相征收关税。

sentences.en: The original idea was they were almost going to be a big free trade zone,
sentences.zh: 最初的想法是它们几乎要成为一个巨大的自由贸易区，

sentences.en: but that breaks down fairly quickly.
sentences.zh: 但这很快就破裂了。

sentences.en: The economy falls into recession.
sentences.zh: 经济陷入衰退。

sentences.en: Economists disagree about exactly how severe it was.
sentences.zh: 经济学家们对于它到底有多严重存在分歧。

sentences.en: Some say it was even worse than the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 有些人说它甚至比大萧条还要糟糕。

sentences.en: Many say it was much less severe.
sentences.zh: 许多人说它没那么严重。

sentences.en: But in any case, people at the time thought it was a pretty bad problem.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，当时的人们认为这是一个相当严重的问题。

sentences.en: So there are all these different things going on.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些不同的事情都在发生。

sentences.en: And that's why Washington is mortified beyond expression.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么华盛顿感到无法言表的羞愧。

sentences.en: So there are certainly, there's a lot of political conflict as well,
sentences.zh: 所以当然，也有很多政治冲突，

sentences.en: but I think it's even, it's a deeper question.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这甚至是一个更深层的问题。

sentences.en: In fact, he goes on and he said that he's mortified beyond expression,
sentences.zh: 事实上，他继续说道，他感到无法言表的羞愧，

sentences.en: that at the moment of our acknowledged independence,
sentences.zh: 在我们承认独立的时刻，

sentences.en: we look ridiculous and contemptible in the eyes of all Europe.
sentences.zh: 我们在整个欧洲眼中看起来荒谬且令人鄙视。

sentences.en: And so what he's saying is we've founded this country and it's falling apart.
sentences.zh: 所以他的意思是，我们建立了这个国家，而它正在分崩离析。

sentences.en: So as the states are wrangling with one another and we're trying to figure out whether to actually have
sentences.zh: 因此，当各州互相争吵，我们试图弄清楚是否真的要拥有

sentences.en: a workable federal government, it turns out that the states come up with something of a compromise
sentences.zh: 一个可行的联邦政府时，事实证明各州达成了一种妥协，

sentences.en: in terms of how to build the institutions of what today we think of as the modern federal government.
sentences.zh: 即如何建立我们今天认为是现代联邦政府的机构。

sentences.en: So look, one of the first debates was how do you build Congress?
sentences.zh: 所以，你看，最初的辩论之一是如何建立国会？

sentences.en: The small states wanted a Congress that would represent them one vote per state.
sentences.zh: 小州想要一个代表它们的国会，每个州一票。

sentences.en: So a state like Delaware or New Hampshire would want that.
sentences.zh: 所以像特拉华州或新罕布什尔州这样的州会想要那样。

sentences.en: But other states, the large states, wanted proportional representation,
sentences.zh: 但其他州，大州，想要比例代表制，

sentences.en: representation according to the number of voters.
sentences.zh: 根据选民人数进行代表分配。

sentences.en: But in any case, as they were trying to figure out how to set up Congress,
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，当他们试图弄清楚如何建立国会时，

sentences.en: they came up with an interesting compromise, which we all know is the Great Compromise,
sentences.zh: 他们达成了一个有趣的妥协，我们都知道这是“大妥协”，

sentences.en: is where they set up the House of Representatives, as you well know,
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，他们建立了众议院，

sentences.en: is going to be organized by proportional representation.
sentences.zh: 将按比例代表制组织。

sentences.en: And the Senate is going to be two votes per state.
sentences.zh: 而参议院将是每个州两票。

sentences.en: But what's particularly interesting about this is that I think often people think about compromise.
sentences.zh: 但特别有趣的是，我认为人们经常想到妥协。

sentences.en: And we think, and you hear this all the time today,
sentences.zh: 我们认为，而且你今天经常听到这个词，

sentences.en: oh, we need to compromise, we need to meet in the middle.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们需要妥协，我们需要在中间地带会合。

sentences.en: Meeting in the middle is one form of compromise, it occurs sometimes.
sentences.zh: 在中间地带会合是一种妥协形式，有时会发生。

sentences.en: But I think even more common, I think, in American history in dealing with the kind of conflict that I see
sentences.zh: 但我认为在美国历史中，在处理我所看到的这种冲突时，更常见的是

sentences.en: is that you don't meet in the middle, you do sort of the best of both,
sentences.zh: 你不是在中间地带会合，你做的是两者的最佳结合，

sentences.en: the best of one idea and the best of another.
sentences.zh: 一个想法的精华和另一个想法的精华。

sentences.en: So what you see is the small states got what they wanted and the large states got what they wanted.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到的是小州得到了它们想要的，大州也得到了它们想要的。

sentences.en: So instead of meeting in the middle or splitting the difference, they did both.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有在中间会合或折中，而是两者兼顾。

sentences.en: So the historical moment that mortified Washington also resulted in a model of government
sentences.zh: 因此，那个让华盛顿感到羞愧的历史时刻，也产生了一种政府模式，

sentences.en: that has endured for more than two centuries.
sentences.zh: 这种模式已经持续了两个多世纪。

sentences.en: The conflict was painful, but productive.
sentences.zh: 冲突是痛苦的，但也是富有成效的。

sentences.en: Nearly 100 years later, the new nation was tested again,
sentences.zh: 近100年后，新国家再次受到考验，

sentences.en: this time after the election of Abraham Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 这一次是在亚伯拉罕·林肯当选之后。

sentences.en: Let the consequences be what they may, whether the Potomac is crimsoned in human gore,
sentences.zh: 无论后果如何，无论波托马克河是否被人类的鲜血染红，

sentences.en: and Pennsylvania Avenue is paved ten fathoms in depth with mangled bodies,
sentences.zh: 无论宾夕法尼亚大道是否被残缺的尸体铺满十英寻深，

sentences.en: or whether the last vestige of liberty is swept from the face of the American continent.
sentences.zh: 还是自由的最后一点痕迹是否从美洲大陆的表面被扫除。

sentences.en: The South will never submit to such humiliation and degradation as the inauguration of Abraham Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 南方永远不会屈服于亚伯拉罕·林肯就职典礼这样的羞辱和堕落。

sentences.en: An Atlanta newspaper expressed what many were feeling in the country at the time.
sentences.zh: 一家亚特兰大的报纸表达了当时全国许多人的感受。

sentences.en: Southern states were starting to secede.
sentences.zh: 南方各州开始脱离联邦。

sentences.en: It was the eve of the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 那是内战的前夜。

sentences.en: While the Civil War brought slavery to an end,
sentences.zh: 虽然内战终结了奴隶制，

sentences.en: David still thinks of this moment as an example of destructive conflict.
sentences.zh: 大卫仍然认为这一时刻是破坏性冲突的一个例子。

sentences.en: That's because the conflict wasn't resolved through the democratic process,
sentences.zh: 那是因为这场冲突并非通过民主程序解决，

sentences.en: but through the bloodiest war in American history.
sentences.zh: 而是通过美国历史上最血腥的战争解决的。

sentences.en: When you look at productive conflict, what you see is that although the two sides disagree vehemently
sentences.zh: 当你审视建设性冲突时，你会发现，尽管双方在某些议题或问题上存在激烈分歧，

sentences.en: about some issue or problem, they do have something in common.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实有共同之处。

sentences.en: And what you see again and again is Americans have believed deeply in their political system,
sentences.zh: 你一次又一次地看到，美国人对他们的政治制度、

sentences.en: in their democracy.

sentences.zh: 但它异常坚韧，并产生了巨大的进步，

sentences.en: economic progress, social progress, political, a lot slower than we'd all like.
sentences.zh: 经济进步、社会进步、政治进步，尽管比我们所有人希望的要慢得多。

sentences.en: But, boy, things can go very badly, and we all know that.
sentences.zh: 但是，天哪，事情可能会变得非常糟糕，我们都知道这一点。

sentences.en: And so the question is, can you continue to make progress?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，你能继续取得进步吗？

sentences.en: So which of these historical analogies describes the current moment in the United States?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些历史类比中哪一个描述了美国当前的时刻？

sentences.en: Are we on the brink of a new chapter in our democracy, or on the brink of divorce?
sentences.zh: 我们是处于民主新篇章的边缘，还是处于分裂的边缘？

sentences.en: I asked David about a number of more recent developments
sentences.zh: 我问了大卫一些最近的发展情况，

sentences.en: that raise troubling signals about the health of our democracy.
sentences.zh: 这些发展引发了对我们民主健康状况的担忧信号。

sentences.en: He's still questioning the authenticity of President Barack Obama's birth certificate.
sentences.zh: 他仍然在质疑巴拉克·奥巴马总统出生证明的真实性。

sentences.en: Very simple.
sentences.zh: 非常简单。

sentences.en: I have people looking into it.
sentences.zh: 我让人在调查这件事。

sentences.en: We're introducing articles of impeachment to remove President Trump from office.
sentences.zh: 我们正在提出弹劾条款，以罢免特朗普总统的职务。

sentences.en: Given the magnitude of the constitutional crisis, there's no reason for divorce.
sentences.zh: 考虑到宪法危机的严重性，没有理由分裂。

sentences.en: This is not based on any real theories of law.
sentences.zh: 这并非基于任何真正的法律理论。

sentences.en: This is the congressional equivalent of petulant children throwing a temper tantrum because their team loSt.
sentences.zh: 这相当于国会里任性的孩子因为他们的队伍输了而发脾气。

sentences.en: Are these modern conflicts business as usual?
sentences.zh: 这些现代冲突是常态吗？

sentences.en: Or has something changed?
sentences.zh: 还是发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: I think both.
sentences.zh: 我认为两者都有。

sentences.en: I mean, it depends what you want the comparison to be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这取决于你想做什么样的比较。

sentences.en: I think that relative to much of the 20th century, we've been more partisan.
sentences.zh: 我认为相对于20世纪的大部分时间，我们变得更加党派化了。

sentences.en: We're more partisan today than in a long time.
sentences.zh: 我们今天比很长一段时间以来都更加党派化。

sentences.en: But I have to say, if you look back in the 19th century, there were strong divisions, very powerful divisions.
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，如果你回顾19世纪，那时存在着强烈的、非常强大的分歧。

sentences.en: At one moment, that, of course, led to the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 当然，在某一时刻，这导致了内战。

sentences.en: But most of the time, those divisions actually did not lead to anything like violence.
sentences.zh: 但大多数时候，这些分歧实际上并没有导致任何类似暴力的事情。

sentences.en: In fact, they often led to very productive conflict.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它们往往导致了非常有建设性的冲突。

sentences.en: So I don't think the question, I don't think the right question is, is there too much conflict?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为问题不在于，我不认为正确的问题是：冲突是否太多了？

sentences.en: Again, I think conflict, especially if it stays in the political realm, is a very good thing.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我认为冲突，特别是如果它保持在政治领域内，是一件非常好的事情。

sentences.en: It generates good ideas.
sentences.zh: 它能产生好的想法。

sentences.en: The question is, what do we have in common?
sentences.zh: 问题是，我们有什么共同点？

sentences.en: I think that's really, we have to ask ourselves, not how do we suppress conflict, but how do we elevate what we have in common?
sentences.zh: 我认为这才是我们必须问自己的，不是我们如何压制冲突，而是我们如何提升我们的共同点？

sentences.en: So we don't have a common ethnic origin.
sentences.zh: 我们没有共同的种族起源。

sentences.en: We don't have a common religion.
sentences.zh: 我们没有共同的宗教。

sentences.en: This country is very different from many others.
sentences.zh: 这个国家与许多其他国家非常不同。

sentences.en: We have people coming from all over.
sentences.zh: 我们有来自世界各地的人。

sentences.en: What we've had from the beginning is, I hope, is a common faith in small d, not the party, but the system, democratic,
sentences.zh: 从一开始我们就拥有的，我希望是，对小写的d（民主），不是指政党，而是指制度，民主的信仰，

sentences.en: or you can call it small r, republican governance.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以称之为小写的r（共和），共和治理。

sentences.en: And this actually, Benjamin Franklin, one of the greatest minds this country ever produced,
sentences.zh: 而这实际上，本杰明·富兰克林，这个国家有史以来最伟大的头脑之一，

sentences.en: back in 1776, the Continental Congress, just hours after it adopted the Declaration of Independence,
sentences.zh: 早在1776年，大陆会议在通过《独立宣言》仅几小时后，

sentences.en: it asked a very powerful, heavyweight group of people, John Adams, Thomas Jefferson, and Ben Franklin,
sentences.zh: 就要求一个非常有影响力、重量级的人群，约翰·亚当斯、托马斯·杰斐逊和本·富兰克林，

sentences.en: to develop a seal for the United States of America, the Great Seal, a two-sided emblem.
sentences.zh: 为美利坚合众国设计一枚印章，即国玺，一个双面徽章。

sentences.en: They wanted some marketing materials for this new country they had just formed.
sentences.zh: 他们想为这个刚刚成立的新国家制作一些宣传材料。

sentences.en: And anyway, these three come up with a design, and Congress doesn't like it.
sentences.zh: 总之，这三个人提出了一个设计，但国会不喜欢。

sentences.en: They reject it.
sentences.zh: 他们拒绝了。

sentences.en: They come up with another design.
sentences.zh: 他们又提出了另一个设计。

sentences.en: But Franklin, in that process, came up with three words that Congress did like.
sentences.zh: 但在那个过程中，富兰克林想出了三个国会喜欢的词。

sentences.en: And those three words were Latin words, e pluribus unum.
sentences.zh: 那三个词是拉丁语，E pluribus unum（合众为一）。

sentences.en: He took those words not from a great Roman thinker, but rather from a magazine he liked called Gentleman's Magazine.
sentences.zh: 他采用这些词不是来自一位伟大的罗马思想家，而是来自他喜欢的一本名为《绅士杂志》的杂志。

sentences.en: It was a literary magazine.
sentences.zh: 那是一本文学杂志。

sentences.en: And on the cover were these words, e pluribus unum, out of many, one.
sentences.zh: 封面上写着这些词，E pluribus unum，合众为一。

sentences.en: And what they were trying to say in the magazine was, out of many literary works,
sentences.zh: 杂志里想表达的意思是，从许多文学作品中，

sentences.en: they brought together many fragments of literary works, out of many fragments of literary works, one magazine.
sentences.zh: 他们汇集了许多文学作品的片段，从许多文学作品的片段中，汇成一本杂志。

sentences.en: What he saw it as, out of many states and peoples, one nation.
sentences.zh: 他将其视为，从许多州和人民中，汇成一个国家。

sentences.en: And I think what he understood really very early was that diversity, difference, created great strengths for the country.
sentences.zh: 我认为他很早就明白，多样性和差异性为这个国家创造了巨大的力量。

sentences.en: But what was going to create that unity?
sentences.zh: 但什么能创造那种统一呢？

sentences.en: It was going to be our belief, our common belief in democratic self-governance, or he would have called it republican self-governance.
sentences.zh: 那将是我们的信仰，我们对民主自治的共同信仰，或者他会称之为共和自治。

sentences.en: And so I think that that's just immensely important.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这极其重要。

sentences.en: So as we look at conflict, I think it's maybe a fool's errand to try to suppress conflict.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们审视冲突时，我认为试图压制冲突可能是一种徒劳。

sentences.en: The question is, do we have enough in common to hold it together?
sentences.zh: 问题是，我们是否有足够的共同点来维持团结？

sentences.en: Political scientists have noticed that both parties are becoming more ideologically consistent.
sentences.zh: 政治学家注意到，两党在意识形态上都变得更加一致。

sentences.en: In other words, Republicans are more conservative, and Democrats are more liberal than they used to be.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，共和党人比过去更保守，民主党人比过去更自由。

sentences.en: I asked David if this kind of polarization might be leading to destructive conflict.
sentences.zh: 我问大卫，这种极化是否可能导致破坏性冲突。

sentences.en: Look, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 看，我们不知道。

sentences.en: So I want to be careful.
sentences.zh: 所以我得小心点。

sentences.en: I'm a historian.
sentences.zh: 我是个历史学家。

sentences.en: I look backwards.
sentences.zh: 我回顾过去。

sentences.en: I'm not so good at predicting the future, and I think none of us are.
sentences.zh: 我不擅长预测未来，我想我们谁都不擅长。

sentences.en: So we don't know if this type of conflict is itself dangerous.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不知道这种冲突本身是否危险。

sentences.en: I guess I'm not convinced that it is.
sentences.zh: 我想我并不确信它是。

sentences.en: I think a much bigger concern, and if you look at, for example,
sentences.zh: 我认为一个更大的担忧是，如果你看看，例如，

sentences.en: Gallup asked this question on a regular basis, if you ask, do you have confidence in your fellow
sentences.zh: 盖洛普定期问这个问题，如果你问，你是否有信心你的美国同胞

sentences.en: Americans to make decisions as part of our democracy, actually, that number has been falling
sentences.zh: 能作为我们民主的一部分做出决定，实际上，这个数字一直在下降，

sentences.en: quite dramatically.
sentences.zh: 而且下降得相当剧烈。

sentences.en: And the number who say that they have little or no confidence in their fellow Americans
sentences.zh: 而那些说他们对美国同胞几乎没有或根本没有信心的人数，

sentences.en: has increased sharply from about 15% in the early 1970s to about 43% today.
sentences.zh: 从20世纪70年代初的约15%急剧增加到今天的约43%。

sentences.en: Those are big numbers.
sentences.zh: 这些数字很大。

sentences.en: I have to say I worry much more about those numbers than ideological conformity and so on.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我比担心意识形态的一致性等等更担心这些数字。

sentences.en: I think the question is, do you have some faith in those around you?
sentences.zh: 我认为问题是，你对周围的人有信心吗？

sentences.en: Even if you disagree with them sharply, do you believe in the system?
sentences.zh: 即使你与他们有严重分歧，你相信这个制度吗？

sentences.en: Are you willing, when you lose, to accept it?
sentences.zh: 当你输了的时候，你愿意接受吗？

sentences.en: And are you going to be treated with some degree of respect when you lose as well?
sentences.zh: 当你输了的时候，你也会受到一定程度的尊重吗？

sentences.en: You know, as we think about winning and losing, we have to lose with grace, and we have to win
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们思考赢和输时，我们必须优雅地输，我们也必须

sentences.en: with grace as well.
sentences.zh: 优雅地赢。

sentences.en: And maybe we just have to be careful not to let the winning and losing become a value of its own.
sentences.zh: 也许我们只是需要小心，不要让输赢本身成为一种价值。

sentences.en: As I was talking to David, I thought of a wicked joke.
sentences.zh: 当我和大卫交谈时，我想到了一个刻薄的笑话。

sentences.en: A man falls off the top of a 100-story building.
sentences.zh: 一个人从100层楼的顶上掉下来。

sentences.en: As he's falling, he passes the 20th floor, and he tells himself, well, everything seems
sentences.zh: 当他下落时，他经过20楼，他告诉自己，嗯，到目前为止一切似乎

sentences.en: to be going pretty well so far.
sentences.zh: 都进行得相当顺利。

sentences.en: David's take on history is that the United States is resilient.
sentences.zh: 大卫对历史的看法是，美国是坚韧的。

sentences.en: We've had a lot of setbacks and crises, and none of them has proved fatal.
sentences.zh: 我们经历了很多挫折和危机，但没有一个被证明是致命的。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'm going to ask David how we can know if our present moment is just
sentences.zh: 回来后，我要问大卫，我们怎么知道我们现在的时刻是否只是

sentences.en: one of those false alarms, or whether it's an example of that guy who's about to go splat.
sentences.zh: 那些虚惊一场的例子之一，还是那个即将摔成肉饼的人的例子。

sentences.en: Social scientists talk about two sets of problems when you're looking at phenomena.
sentences.zh: 社会科学家在观察现象时会谈论两类问题。

sentences.en: They talk about things that are false positives and things that are false negatives.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论假阳性和假阴性。

sentences.en: So the false positives are things that look like alarm bells, and, you know, if you pay
sentences.zh: 所以假阳性是那些看起来像警钟的事情，而且，你知道，如果你给予

sentences.en: too much attention to them, you will chase all sorts of little things down rabbit holes, and
sentences.zh: 太多关注，你就会钻进各种各样的牛角尖，

sentences.en: most of them will come to nothing.
sentences.zh: 而大多数都不会有什么结果。

sentences.en: If you ignore the false negatives, they're the things that you miss that actually turn
sentences.zh: 如果你忽视了假阴性，它们就是你错过的、实际上最终

sentences.en: out to be catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 演变成灾难的事情。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, as you're thinking about the long sweep of history, it's clear there
sentences.zh: 我想知道，当你思考漫长的历史进程时，很明显

sentences.en: have been many, many, many examples of false positives where you sort of said things look
sentences.zh: 有许多、许多、许多假阳性的例子，你当时说事情看起来

sentences.en: like they're coming apart, things look like they're falling apart, and they haven't.
sentences.zh: 好像要分崩离析，事情看起来好像要崩溃，但它们并没有。

sentences.en: And the case you make as a result is that the country is resilient.
sentences.zh: 而你因此得出的结论是，这个国家是坚韧的。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering if this belief in our resilience can hide the fact that sometimes
sentences.zh: 但我怀疑这种对我们韧性的信念是否会掩盖这样一个事实：有时

sentences.en: actually we might be at risk.
sentences.zh: 实际上我们可能处于危险之中。

sentences.en: In other words, it's only in hindsight that you know that a certain thing turned out well
sentences.zh: 换句话说，只有事后回顾，你才知道某件事结果是好

sentences.en: or badly.
sentences.zh: 还是坏。

sentences.en: In the moment, how do you know which way it's going to go?
sentences.zh: 在当下，你怎么知道它会走向何方？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you said that, you know, people have been seeing the collapse of American democracy
sentences.zh: 所以你说，你知道，人们已经看到美国民主的崩溃

sentences.en: for a very, very long time.
sentences.zh: 已经有很长很长一段时间了。

sentences.en: You know, when James Madison was elected, a fiercely federalist newspaper in Connecticut
sentences.zh: 你知道，当詹姆斯·麦迪逊当选时，康涅狄格州一家激进的联邦党报纸

sentences.en: said that the country was fast on the broad road to despotism and ruin.
sentences.zh: 说这个国家正快速走在通往专制和毁灭的大道上。

sentences.en: So these things have happened before.
sentences.zh: 所以这些事情以前也发生过。

sentences.en: And the critics, as you say, the critics are usually wrong.
sentences.zh: 而且正如你所说，批评者通常是错的。

sentences.en: In one moment, they weren't, right, in the lead up to the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 但在某一时刻，他们没错，对吧，在内战前夕。

sentences.en: We can't just take comfort in the fact that many, many times people have said democracy was
sentences.zh: 我们不能仅仅因为很多人多次说民主正在失败，

sentences.en: failing and many, many times they were wrong.
sentences.zh: 而他们多次都错了，就感到安慰。

sentences.en: Because if we do that, what if this is one of the times when they're right?
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们这样做，万一这次他们是对的呢？

sentences.en: So you're asking the question, how can you tell the difference?
sentences.zh: 所以你在问这个问题，你怎么能分辨出区别？

sentences.en: I think you need to look at, is the culture of democracy strong enough to hold us together?
sentences.zh: 我认为你需要看看，民主文化是否足够强大以维持我们的团结？

sentences.en: That's the question I keep asking.
sentences.zh: 这是我不断在问的问题。

sentences.en: How do you know?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道？

sentences.en: You need to look at your politicians.
sentences.zh: 你需要看看你的政客们。

sentences.en: Look at the ones on your side who agree with you.
sentences.zh: 看看你那一边同意你观点的人。

sentences.en: And do you see them ever putting democracy in second place?
sentences.zh: 你是否见过他们把民主放在第二位？

sentences.en: And how often do they do it?
sentences.zh: 他们多久做一次？

sentences.en: So I'll leave it to listeners to make that decision.
sentences.zh: 所以我把这个决定留给听众。

sentences.en: My guess is you can find some examples of that.
sentences.zh: 我猜你可以找到一些相关的例子。

sentences.en: And you can find examples in history.
sentences.zh: 你也可以在历史中找到例子。

sentences.en: The more severe that becomes, the more dangerous it becomes.
sentences.zh: 这种情况越严重，就越危险。

sentences.en: It's good, I think, in a democracy to be hypochondriacs.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在民主国家里，有点“疑病症”其实是好事。

sentences.en: That is, to think that, oh, our system might be sick.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，会去想：噢，我们的体制是不是生病了。

sentences.en: Because when you think it might be sick, you start to take some action to try to fix it.
sentences.zh: 因为当你认为它可能生病时，你就会开始采取行动去尝试修复它。

sentences.en: And you see that it's in moments of political reform that you do have almost like a national
sentences.zh: 你会发现，正是在政治改革的时刻，你才会有某种类似于国民

sentences.en: civics class.
sentences.zh: 公民课的体验。

sentences.en: You do get people talking about democracy, thinking about principles.
sentences.zh: 人们确实会开始讨论民主，思考原则。

sentences.en: The civil rights movement, the voting rights movement that we talked about before and leading
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到的民权运动、投票权运动，以及最终促成

sentences.en: up to the 1965 Voting Rights Act.
sentences.zh: 1965年《投票权法案》的过程。

sentences.en: That was such a time.
sentences.zh: 那确实是那样的时期。

sentences.en: It was like a national civics class.
sentences.zh: 就像一堂国民公民课。

sentences.en: And so where people were thinking about these, what does equal protection mean?
sentences.zh: 人们当时在思考这些问题：平等保护意味着什么？

sentences.en: Are we following it?
sentences.zh: 我们是否在遵循它？

sentences.en: Are we not following it?
sentences.zh: 我们是否没有遵循它？

sentences.en: So we need to think about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要思考这些问题。

sentences.en: And if we can maybe just get away a little bit from only talking about, should taxes be
sentences.zh: 如果我们能稍微跳出那种只谈论“税收应该

sentences.en: high or low?
sentences.zh: 高还是低”的思维，

sentences.en: Should government be big or small?
sentences.zh: “政府应该大还是小”的思维，

sentences.en: Should guns be protected this way or not protected or so on?
sentences.zh: “枪支应该这样保护还是不保护”等等，

sentences.en: All those fights are important fights, extremely important.
sentences.zh: 所有这些争论都很重要，极其重要。

sentences.en: But we can't only fight about that.
sentences.zh: 但我们不能只争论这些。

sentences.en: We need to think about sort of the broader pillars of government and make sure we understand
sentences.zh: 我们需要思考政府更广泛的支柱，确保我们理解

sentences.en: them and make sure we retain our commitment to them.
sentences.zh: 它们，并确保我们保持对它们的承诺。

sentences.en: One of the other factors you identify that's different about partisanship today from partisanship
sentences.zh: 你指出的当今党派之争与过去党派之争不同的另一个因素是，你说过去的党派之争更具活力，

sentences.en: in the past is that you say partisanship in the past was more exuberant, that things
sentences.zh: 而今天的事情

sentences.en: were more cynical today rather than exuberant.
sentences.zh: 更多是愤世嫉俗，而不是充满活力。

sentences.en: What do you mean by exuberant partisanship and how could we bring that back?
sentences.zh: 你所说的“充满活力的党派之争”是什么意思？我们该如何找回那种活力？

sentences.en: One of the things I write about in the book is, particularly in the conclusion, is this
sentences.zh: 我在书中写到的一点，特别是在结论中，就是

sentences.en: is what appears to be a decline in this culture of democracy.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是民主文化的一种衰落。

sentences.en: And one element of that actually goes back a very long way.
sentences.zh: 而其中的一个因素其实由来已久。

sentences.en: It's not just recent.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是最近才发生的。

sentences.en: So as you say, I think if you go back into the 19th century, partisanship was extremely,
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我认为如果你回到19世纪，党派之争极其、

sentences.en: extremely strong.
sentences.zh: 极其强烈。

sentences.en: But there was a life in it and excitement.
sentences.zh: 但其中充满了生命力和兴奋感。

sentences.en: You use the word exuberance.
sentences.zh: 你用了“活力”这个词。

sentences.en: I think that's a good one.
sentences.zh: 我觉得用得很好。

sentences.en: And that came out, for example, beautifully on Election Day.
sentences.zh: 例如，这在选举日表现得淋漓尽致。

sentences.en: Election Day was a celebration.
sentences.zh: 选举日曾是一场庆典。

sentences.en: It was a party.
sentences.zh: 那是一场派对。

sentences.en: It was completely different from Election Day today.
sentences.zh: 它与今天的选举日完全不同。

sentences.en: What do I mean by that?
sentences.zh: 我这是什么意思呢？

sentences.en: Well, back then, actually, voting was public.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那时投票实际上是公开的。

sentences.en: So this was before the secret ballot.
sentences.zh: 那是在秘密投票制度出现之前。

sentences.en: You would go and cast a ballot.
sentences.zh: 你会去投下一张选票。

sentences.en: Your ballot usually had a color.
sentences.zh: 你的选票通常是有颜色的。

sentences.en: It might be pink.
sentences.zh: 可能是粉色的。

sentences.en: It might be blue.
sentences.zh: 可能是蓝色的。

sentences.en: And it would reflect what party you were voting for.
sentences.zh: 它会反映出你投的是哪个党派。

sentences.en: Everyone could see when you put the ballot in.
sentences.zh: 当你放入选票时，每个人都能看到。

sentences.en: And there were a lot of people around you.
sentences.zh: 而且你周围有很多很多人。

sentences.en: In fact, usually at your voting place, there was a celebration going on.
sentences.zh: 事实上，通常在你的投票点，正在举行一场庆祝活动。

sentences.en: There was a lot of debating.
sentences.zh: 有很多辩论。

sentences.en: There was a lot of drinking.
sentences.zh: 有很多喝酒的人。

sentences.en: There was a lot of fighting.
sentences.zh: 有很多打架的人。

sentences.en: There was a lot going on.
sentences.zh: 现场非常热闹。

sentences.en: And some people were actually afraid to go vote because it was such a raucous environment.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至因为环境太嘈杂而不敢去投票。

sentences.en: But overall, the voting rates were up at 70%, 75%, 80%.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，投票率高达70%、75%、80%。

sentences.en: So very high voting rates, much higher than we have today.
sentences.zh: 所以投票率非常高，远高于我们今天的情况。

sentences.en: So there was this celebratory atmosphere that was going on at every Election Day.
sentences.zh: 因此，每个选举日都有一种庆祝的氛围。

sentences.en: And part of that was something we wouldn't want to repeat.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分是我们不想重演的。

sentences.en: So, you know, why were ballots so public?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，为什么选票要那么公开？

sentences.en: Why was voting so public?
sentences.zh: 为什么投票要那么公开？

sentences.en: Well, part of it was political machines wanted to be able to pay people off to vote for their party.
sentences.zh: 嗯，部分原因是政治机器想要能够收买人们去投他们党的票。

sentences.en: And you couldn't really pay people off if you couldn't see how they were going to vote.
sentences.zh: 如果你看不到人们怎么投票，你就无法真正收买他们。

sentences.en: So if you're going to pay them a dollar to vote this way or that, you had to make sure you knew how they're actually going to vote.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你要付他们一美元让他们投这个或那个，你必须确保你知道他们实际上是怎么投的。

sentences.en: So you had to see, you had to have someone at the polling place watch them put the vote in.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须看到，你必须在投票站有人盯着他们把票投进去。

sentences.en: So there was a downside.
sentences.zh: 所以这有一个负面影响。

sentences.en: There was a corruption associated with this old system.
sentences.zh: 这种旧制度伴随着腐败。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, when we fixed that, we ended up taking the life out of voting.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，当我们修复了这一点时，我们最终也抽离了投票的生命力。

sentences.en: And now most people go, they vote, they vote in a private booth, and they make their decision.
sentences.zh: 现在大多数人去投票，他们在私密的投票间里投票，做出他们的决定。

sentences.en: They walk out, they maybe buy a brownie at a bake sale or something.
sentences.zh: 他们走出来，可能在义卖活动上买个布朗尼蛋糕之类的。

sentences.en: And that's about it.
sentences.zh: 差不多就是这样了。

sentences.en: There's not really much engagement.
sentences.zh: 真的没有什么参与感。

sentences.en: There's certainly not a lot of debating.
sentences.zh: 当然也没有什么辩论。

sentences.en: There's not a lot of drinking.
sentences.zh: 没有多少喝酒的人。

sentences.en: And there's maybe, fortunately, not a lot of fighting, physical fighting.
sentences.zh: 而且幸运的是，可能也没有多少打架，那种肢体冲突。

sentences.en: But there is a question.
sentences.zh: 但有一个问题。

sentences.en: Could we have a little bit more of that celebratory atmosphere?
sentences.zh: 我们能不能多一点那种庆祝的氛围？

sentences.en: Could Election Day be a holiday?
sentences.zh: 选举日能不能成为一个节日？

sentences.en: Could it be more of a celebration?
sentences.zh: 它能不能更像是一场庆典？

sentences.en: And what you'd see is a lot more people engaged in the democracy.
sentences.zh: 你会看到更多的人参与到民主中来。

sentences.en: And it was an important moment.
sentences.zh: 那是一个重要的时刻。

sentences.en: So we lost that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们失去了这一点。

sentences.en: We got something in return.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了一些回报。

sentences.en: We got a cleaner electoral system.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了一个更干净的选举制度。

sentences.en: I wouldn't want to give that up.
sentences.zh: 我不想放弃这一点。

sentences.en: But, boy, we lost something in the process.
sentences.zh: 但是，天哪，我们在过程中确实失去了一些东西。

sentences.en: When I look at the present moment, just in the last few months,
sentences.zh: 当我审视当下，就在过去几个月里，

sentences.en: it feels like I've seen numerous pictures of liberals and Democrats holding up signs to Donald Trump saying,
sentences.zh: 我感觉我看到了无数自由派和民主党人举着牌子对唐纳德·特朗普说，

sentences.en: not my president.
sentences.zh: 他不是我的总统。

sentences.en: He's not my president.
sentences.zh: 他不是我的总统。

sentences.en: Deeply unhappy about how the election turned out, but not just unhappy, to the point of saying,
sentences.zh: 对选举结果深感不满，但不仅仅是不满，甚至到了说

sentences.en: he is not a legitimate president.
sentences.zh: 他不是一位合法的总统的地步。

sentences.en: When you look at the conflict we're having right now about whether Russia interfered with the presidential election,
sentences.zh: 当你审视我们现在关于俄罗斯是否干预了总统选举的冲突时，

sentences.en: there is real division among Republicans.
sentences.zh: 共和党内部确实存在分歧。

sentences.en: Is this, are we supposed to be defending the president and approaching this from a partisan point of view?
sentences.zh: 这是……我们应该捍卫总统并从党派的角度来看待这件事吗？

sentences.en: Or are we supposed to be thinking about this as Americans worried about, you know, foreign power trying to influence our democracy?
sentences.zh: 还是我们应该以美国人的身份来思考这个问题，担心外国势力试图影响我们的民主？

sentences.en: I think both of those are pretty clear examples that lots of people are placing party before country.
sentences.zh: 我认为这两者都是非常明显的例子，说明许多人把党派利益置于国家利益之上。

sentences.en: I think it depends how far it goes.
sentences.zh: 我认为这取决于它发展到什么程度。

sentences.en: So certainly, you know, you gave the example of many people are out there saying Trump isn't my president.
sentences.zh: 当然，你举了很多人在外面说“特朗普不是我的总统”的例子。

sentences.en: You know, the same was true of Barack Obama, that many people didn't think he was a legitimate president.
sentences.zh: 你知道，巴拉克·奥巴马也是如此，许多人认为他不是一位合法的总统。

sentences.en: I think the question, though, is to what extent are you then willing to violate the law because you think there is no law?
sentences.zh: 但我认为问题在于，你愿意在多大程度上因为认为没有法律而违反法律？

sentences.en: And so I think that would be crossing a barrier.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为那将是越过界限。

sentences.en: And so the truth is you can disagree with, for example, either president's executive orders, and you can take them to court.
sentences.zh: 事实是，你可以不同意，例如，任何一位总统的行政命令，你可以诉诸法庭。

sentences.en: The question is, what do you do if you lose in court?
sentences.zh: 问题是，如果你在法庭上输了怎么办？

sentences.en: And what do you do, is court kind of the proper remedy?
sentences.zh: 你该怎么办？法庭是合适的补救措施吗？

sentences.en: I would say if you believe in the democracy, it is.
sentences.zh: 我会说，如果你相信民主，那就是。

sentences.en: And, you know, sometimes you lose, and sometimes you lose for a long time.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有时你会输，有时你会输很长一段时间。

sentences.en: So those who lose need to try to respect the process, fight as hard as they can.
sentences.zh: 所以那些输了的人需要尝试尊重这个过程，尽他们最大的努力去抗争。

sentences.en: I'm not trying to say not to fight.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说不要抗争。

sentences.en: Fight as hard as they can.
sentences.zh: 尽他们最大的努力去抗争。

sentences.en: The question is, do you legally respect the process?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你在法律上尊重这个过程吗？

sentences.en: Those who hold up a sign and saying, you know, the president's not my president, I think they're exercising their First Amendment rights.
sentences.zh: 那些举着牌子说“总统不是我的总统”的人，我认为他们是在行使他们的第一修正案权利。

sentences.en: I have to say, that doesn't cause me grave concern.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，这并不会让我感到严重担忧。

sentences.en: The question is, do you then recognize the political process itself as legitimate?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你是否承认政治过程本身是合法的？

sentences.en: I think so far, mostly, I think the answer has been yes.
sentences.zh: 我认为到目前为止，大多数情况下，答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: So I'm not so worried about the signs.
sentences.zh: 所以我并不太担心那些牌子。

sentences.en: I do get concerned, though, about this atrophy.
sentences.zh: 但我确实对这种萎缩感到担忧。

sentences.en: If you look at our culture of democracy, I've given you one piece of data from a Gallup poll.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看我们的民主文化，我给了你盖洛普民意调查中的一个数据点。

sentences.en: I could give you some others.
sentences.zh: 我还可以给你提供其他一些数据。

sentences.en: I think our culture of democracy has weakened.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们的民主文化已经减弱了。

sentences.en: Maybe that's a little bit part of the reason why people are sometimes holding up those signs.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是人们有时会举起那些牌子的部分原因。

sentences.en: But, again, if that glue is coming apart, then I start to worry that are we going to get the best from column A and the best from column B,
sentences.zh: 但同样，如果那种凝聚力正在瓦解，那么我就开始担心，我们还能像在制宪会议以及之后许多次那样，从A栏和B栏中获得最好的结果吗？

sentences.en: like we did at the Constitutional Convention and so many other times after that?
sentences.zh: 还是我们会陷入瘫痪，无法采取行动？

sentences.en: Or are we going to get paralyzed and be unable to act?
sentences.zh: 还是我们会发现一种多数人的暴政？

sentences.en: Or are we going to find a kind of tyranny of the majority?
sentences.zh: 所以这些都是我们政府体制中可能出现的结果。

sentences.en: So these are all possible outcomes in our system of government.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要开始尊重的是生产性张力、生产性冲突的力量，以及作为公民，在某种意义上做到“左右开弓”是多么重要。

sentences.en: What I think we need to come to respect is the power of productive tension, of productive conflict, and how important it is, in a sense, to be ambidextrous as citizens.
sentences.zh: 一方面，我们需要尽可能和平地抗争，以表达我们的观点，不断推动。

sentences.en: On the one hand, we need to be fighting as hard as we can, peacefully, to get our views, to keep pushing.
sentences.zh: 即使在我们失败时，也要不断推动。

sentences.en: Even, you know, when we lose, we keep pushing and pushing.
sentences.zh: 但同时，另一方面，我们需要尊重我们的民主，我们需要尊重它并对它表现出极大的敬畏。

sentences.en: But at the same time, on the other hand, we need to respect our democracy, and we need to respect it and show it great reverence.
